data.title: Tata Steel to acquire 26.6% promoter stake in APL Apollo for ₹15,510 crore
data.description:
Tata Steel will make an open offer to acquire an additional 26 per cent stake in APL Apollo Tubes at ₹2,301.40 a share for a consideration of ₹16,756 crore, as part of a comprehensive transaction to consolidate its downstream steel tubes and colour-coated products businesses under APL Apollo.

The open offer follows Tata Steel’s agreement to acquire the entire 26.6 per cent promoter holding in APL Apollo at ₹2,100 per share for ₹15,510 crore. The combined acquisition will give Tata Steel a significant stake in the listed steel tubes manufacturer and make APL Apollo its vehicle for driving growth in the downstream steel business.

The transactions, subject to regulatory approvals, are expected to be completed in FY27.

In a parallel transaction, Tata Steel has agreed to transfer its entire steel tubes business and its wholly owned subsidiary Tata Steel Colors to APL Apollo for a combined consideration of ₹28,000 crore. This will bring together Tata Steel’s 1.7 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) steel tubes business and 8 lakh tonnes of surface-coated coil capacity with APL Apollo’s existing 5 MTPA capacity.

Following the consolidation, APL Apollo will initially have a combined capacity of 7.5 MTPA across steel tubes and colour-coated products.

The company plans to expand its steel tube capacity by another 3 MTPA and build 5 MTPA of colour-coated capacity over the coming years. Its long-term ambition is to reach 15.5 MTPA by 2035, comprising around 9 MTPA of steel tubes and 6.5 MTPA of colour-coated products.

A key component of the expansion strategy is an exclusive contract manufacturing arrangement with SG Tech Engineering, an entity associated with the APL Apollo promoter group. Under the agreement, SG Tech will establish 5 MTPA of colour-coated manufacturing capacity through modular facilities spread across India. The first 1 MTPA is expected to be commissioned within 24 months.

The asset-light model is expected to help the combined entity expand geographically while limiting capital expenditure. The partnership will also leverage APL Apollo promoters’ experience in developing downstream manufacturing capacities.

APL Apollo will initially fund the ₹28,000-crore acquisition of Tata Steel’s downstream businesses through a combination of acquisition financing and subsequently replace the debt with long-term capitalisation to reduce balance-sheet risks.

Tata Steel expects the combination to generate synergies through improved capacity utilisation, debottlenecking, joint project development, procurement efficiencies and stronger distribution networks. The expanded product portfolio and pan-India presence are also expected to improve profitability and return on capital employed.

TV Narendran, Managing Director and CEO, Tata Steel said the transaction would create a downstream powerhouse with market agility, a strong growth trajectory and a competitive capital expenditure and operating cost structure.

Koushik Chatterjee, Executive Director and Chief Financial Officer said APL Apollo offered an opportunity to accelerate Tata Steel’s expansion in value-added products. The partnership would provide a foundation for building a large colour-coated products business while leveraging the promoter group’s execution capabilities.

The transaction marks a significant shift in Tata Steel’s downstream strategy, with the company seeking to expand its presence in higher-value steel products through a combination of acquisitions, partnerships and asset-light manufacturing.

data.title: WuXi Biologics' U.S. Site in New Jersey Completes Commercial PPQ Campaign
data.description:
CRANBURY, N.J., Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- WuXi Biologics (2269.HK), a leading global Contract Research, Development and Manufacturing Organization (CRDMO), today announced the successful completion of the commercial Process Performance Qualification (PPQ) campaign at MFG18, its drug substance facility in Cranbury, New Jersey. This successful PPQ campaign marks the site's entry into commercial manufacturing and further strengthens the Company's capability to provide clients in the U.S. and globally with high-quality, reliable biomanufacturing services.

The drug substance PPQ campaign supported a bispecific antibody program transferred to the Cranbury site. In preparation for PPQ, the project team leveraged integrated technical expertise and resources across WuXi Biologics' global network to enhance process robustness. Building on this strong technical foundation, the team completed the first PPQ batch under an accelerated timeline.

With this milestone, the Cranbury site has demonstrated its capability to support the commercial manufacturing of complex biologics. This capability is underpinned by WuXi Biologics' best-in-class quality standards, operational excellence, and continuous technology innovation. Complex modalities now account for more than half of the integrated projects on the Company's CRDMO platform. As of June 30, 2026, WuXi Biologics had supported 221 integrated bispecific and multispecific antibody projects, including three at the commercial stage.

Dr. Chris Chen, CEO of WuXi Biologics, said, "This is a major milestone for our U.S. operations and further strengthens the capabilities of our global manufacturing network. Through seamless collaboration between our U.S. sites and broader global network, we provide clients with end-to-end services spanning process development, clinical-to-commercial manufacturing, and testing. We remain committed to helping clients accelerate the delivery of high-quality, life-saving treatments to patients in the U.S. and around the world by enhancing our global capabilities and execution excellence."

WuXi Biologics continues to extend its U.S. presence by integrating its facilities in New Jersey and Massachusetts into a unified network. Following the completion of its commercial PPQ campaign, MFG18 is expected to reach a total capacity of 13,300 liters by 2027. The facility will support up to 4,000 liters per batch, with an annual capacity of up to 95 batches. The Company's DP12 drug product facility in Robbinsville, New Jersey, provides liquid filling for vials and prefilled syringes, with capacity for up to 20,000 doses per batch and 60 batches per year.

In Massachusetts, the Worcester site will further enhance WuXi Biologics' late-stage clinical and commercial manufacturing capacity. To meet rapidly growing demand in the U.S. market, the site's planned manufacturing capacity has been increased to 36,000 liters. Built on a flexible, cost-efficient platform powered by digital automation and high-throughput processing, the MFG11 drug substance facility in Worcester will span more than 200,000 square feet with a maximum batch size of 12,000 liters.

WuXi Biologics' global manufacturing footprint spans the United States, Ireland, Germany, China, and Singapore, with a network of 26 drug substance facilities and 19 drug product facilities. The network provides integrated dual-sourcing solutions across drug substance and drug product, from clinical development through commercial-scale manufacturing. As of June 30, 2026, WuXi Biologics had successfully passed 49 regulatory inspections worldwide, including 23 conducted by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the European Medicines Agency (EMA).

About WuXi Biologics

WuXi Biologics (stock code: 2269.HK) is a leading global Contract Research, Development and Manufacturing Organization (CRDMO) offering end-to-end solutions that enable partners to discover, develop and manufacture biologics – from concept to commercialization – for the benefit of patients worldwide*.

With over 14,000 employees in China, the United States, Ireland, Germany, and Singapore, including experts and scientists in biologics R&D and manufacturing, technology innovation, and operational excellence, WuXi Biologics leverages its technologies and expertise to deliver efficient, cost-effective, and scalable biologics solutions tailored to meet clients' needs. By embedding digital capability and infrastructure across the full biopharmaceutical value chain, the company turns data, computation, and prediction into transparent client experience, faster development, intelligent operations, and more efficient manufacturing. As of June 30, 2026, WuXi Biologics was supporting 1,064 integrated client projects, including 78 in Phase III and 28 in commercial manufacturing, with complex modalities representing more than half of the entire project portfolio.

WuXi Biologics regards sustainability as the cornerstone of long-term business growth. The company continuously drives green technology innovations to offer advanced end-to-end Green CRDMO solutions for its global partners while consistently achieving excellence in Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG). Committed to creating shared value, it collaborates with all stakeholders to foster positive social and environmental impacts and promote responsible practices that empower the entire value chain.

For more information about WuXi Biologics, please visit: www.wuxibiologics.com

data.title: Bitcoin Comes Off Weekend Lows as Dip-Buyers Step in — Market Talk
data.description:
0421 GMT - Bitcoin edges higher in Asia after another punishing selloff over the weekend brought it to its lowest in over two years. The cryptocurrency's rebound shows that buyers were willing to return when the price fell to near $55,000, says Linh Tran at XS.com. But expectations of interest-rate hikes, a still-strong dollar and continued ETF outflows keep the outlook cautious. Over the next few sessions, Tran leans toward Bitcoin trading around $60,000. It will likely struggle to return to the $65,000 area anytime soon. If Bitcoin can hold above $60,000 through the U.S. sessions early this week--especially if ETFs are still seeing outflows--that would show that buying is strong enough to absorb the selling, Tran says. Bitcoin is up 0.6% at $61,236. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)

0412 GMT - The dollar is likely to trade around 160.00 yen throughout 2027, Morgan Stanley says in a note. Elevated Fed terminal-rate pricing and improving risk sentiment should support the dollar against the yen, while repeated verbal intervention by Japanese financial authorities should limit the yen's depreciation, the U.S. bank says. Japan's terms of trade are also expected to improve gradually next year, supporting the yen, Morgan Stanley says. A sustained downtrend in the dollar would require markets to price U.S. disinflation and a subsequent Fed easing cycle with greater conviction, the bank says. The dollar is at Y159.01. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com; @kosakunarioka)

0408 GMT - The Bank of Korea is expected to hike rates on Thursday in a likely unanimous decision, says BofA Global Research in a report. With headline inflation running above 2.5%, the case for the BOK to consider further tightening to contain inflationary pressures remains strong. Korea's widening current account surplus continues to support the won, but persistent selling by foreign equity investors has weighed on the domestic market with the benchmark Kospi struggling to hold above 5000. The BOK's 2027 GDP growth forecast will be a key figure to watch. "An upgrade to above 3.5% would signal a more bullish assessment of the ongoing semiconductor upcycle and potentially point to greater risk of further rate hikes, implying a more hawkish policy stance than we currently expect," it adds. (monica.gupta@wsj.com)

0323 GMT - Singapore's industrial production growth likely moderated in October, reflecting high base effects, DBS economists say in a note. The city-state's output surged by 15% on year during the same period last year, marking its strongest monthly gain in 2025, they note.Robust artificial intelligence-related demand likely supported precision engineering and electronics production, although electronics growth may have moderated, the economists say. DBS expects Singapore's industrial production growth to slow to 1.0% in October from 3.4% in September. The data is due later this week.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)

0240 GMT - The Singapore dollar consolidates against its U.S. counterpart in the Asian session but may be weighed by risk-off sentiment spurred by regional equity-market weakness. There are "concerns over elevated interest rates, persistent inflation pressures and the unwinding of crowded AI-related positions," UOB Global Economics & Markets Research says in a report. Based on technical analysis, however, the U.S. dollar-Singapore dollar pair's upward momentum has faded following its recent pullback, two members of the research team note. The U.S. dollar has probably entered a range-trading phase between S$1.2885 and S$1.2915, they add. The U.S. dollar is little changed at 1.2898 Singapore dollars, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

0229 GMT - Malaysia's exports could continue to remain resilient in 1Q 2027, supported by sustained AI-driven demand for electrical and electronic products and stronger energy shipments, says CGS International economist Mas Aida Che Mansor in a note. Global semiconductor sales are forecast to grow 29% in 2027. Domestic electrical and electronics capacity utilization of 87.7% also points to continued shipment growth despite rising base effects, she reckons. Petroleum and liquefied natural gas exports should provide additional support, driven by regional demand and resilient manufacturing activity in China and the Asean region. However, a sharper slowdown in the U.S. or China, weaker crude oil prices and rising trade protectionism could weigh on shipments, she adds. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)

0206 GMT - There are good reasons to believe that Australia's current housing market downturn is different to the garden variety cyclical downswings of recent decades, says Paul Bloxham, chief economist for Australia at HSBC. The decline so far is already bigger and sharper than the previous ones, while core inflation remains elevated, despite aggressive interest rate increases this year, he adds. Near-term interest rate cuts are not on the agenda while tax changes and the likelihood that global rates will stay high for longer are adding to the grim picture. Bloxham expects a 13% peak-to-trough house price fall. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)

0145 GMT - There could come a moment of acute discomfort for Australia money markets on Wednesday if inflation data for October delivers a higher-than-expected shock. Headline inflation is expected to rise to an uncomfortable 4.7%, but the more important trimmed mean measure is forecast to be little changed, landing at around 3.6% year over year. With recent economic data coming in weak, markets are already starting to price in interest-rate cuts next year, so an upward inflation shock would trigger volatility. Reserve Bank of Australia Gov. Michele Bullock said last week inflation risks remain skewed toward a rise. Central bank rhetoric remains hawkish generally. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)

0125 GMT - The rates shock has likely evolved into a growth shock, two strategists at OCBC Group Research say in a note. The "AI de-risking hits equities, EM carry and metals," the strategists say. Worries over the artificial-intelligence investment cycle have driven equities and U.S. yields lower, shifting the brunt of U.S. dollar strength toward emerging-market currencies, the strategists say. "In the near term, the USD should continue to benefit from hawkish Fed risks and the pressure that tighter global financial conditions place on the rest of the world," the strategists add. The U.S. Dollar Index is little changed at 103.763, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

0108 GMT - Voters in Australia's southern state of Victoria are expected to hand the current Labor government a huge defeat at elections on Saturday. The mood is grim for the party, and if the drubbing is delivered, questions will be asked about what it means for the federal Labor government. It is likely to officially establish the right-wing populist One Nation party as a force that could impact the status quo in the federal arena. History has shown that voters can vote one way at state level and then another at federal elections. But Saturday's poll feels like it will be a watershed in Australian politics and the fallout could have big ramifications.(james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)

0031 GMT - It's becoming increasingly obvious that the Australian economy is slowing quickly and the Reserve Bank of Australia is winning the war to cool aggregate demand and bring inflation down. The latest PMI data is telling in this regard as is the recent sudden jump in unemployment. Still, there's a problem in that inflation remains elevated. The RBA is likely to sit on the sidelines at its policy meeting in December and keep interest rates on hold. With the housing sector in free fall, a sixth interest rate increase now would feel like a step too far. But the inflation data will ensure the central bank remains hawkish in its messaging. The bank won't relax until the inflation trajectory is downward. That's not the case yet. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)

0022 GMT - New Zealand's economic recovery remains intact. Retail sales volumes surged 2.2% on-quarter in 3Q, well above expectations of a 0.5% rise. It was the strongest quarterly pace of growth since December 2021. The increase was broad-based, with eleven out of fifteen industries experiencing an increase in the quarter. Factoring in the data, Goldman Sachs says it has lifted its 3Q GDP forecast by 10 basis points to 0.7% on-quarter. Andrew Boak, chief economist at GS adds that the balance of risks to the forecast is skewed to the upside. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)

data.description: China's earnings outlook continues to soften according to BNP Paribas in a commentary. Aggregate forward 12-month earnings for the 2,170 Chinese companies that the bank tracks have declined in each of the last two consecutive months for the first time since May 2025, the bank says. data.title: California AG Bonta filed lawsuit against OpenAI over model security, public safety
data.description:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta said on Sunday that he had filed a lawsuit against OpenAI earlier in the week "for failing to keep its models secure and putting public safety at risk."

"OpenAI put growth and speed ahead of safety," Bonta wrote in his weekly newsletter on Sunday. "It disregarded red flags and failed to keep its models secure."

"That is why, this week, I filed a lawsuit to hold it accountable," he said, referring to the lawsuit filed by the state on November 16.

In the lawsuit, Bonta accused OpenAI of developing a dangerous product without adequate safety procedures or oversight after reports that its AI models had independently carried out cyberattacks.

data.title: Trump Throws His Weight Behind Jensen Huang’s Return As Nvidia CEO: ‘It Would Be The Best Thing For The Company’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Trump's public backing of Huang would likely add pressure on Nvidia’s board, which last week said it had no plans to reinstate the executive.
  • Just 10 days ago, Trump was calling for Apple’s Tim Cook to replace Huang.
  • Retail sentiment for NVDA was ‘extremely bullish.

President Donald Trump on Sunday backed a proposal for Jensen Huang to return as Nvidia’s CEO, saying it would be good for both the AI chipmaker and the country.

“I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A. President DONALD J. TRUMP,” he posted on his Trump Social account.

NVDA stock gained 6.5% in overnight trading following Trump’s post. It fell 23% last week, its worst drop since September 2008. If the overnight move holds up on Monday, it would be the stock’s best trading day since a post-earnings rally in August.

Trump's public backing of Huang would likely add pressure on Nvidia’s board, which last week said it had no plans to reinstate the executive. Huang was involved in multiple illicit affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, leading to his ouster as well as probes into the AI chipmaker.

Just 10 days ago, Trump was calling for Apple’s Tim Cook to replace Huang.

Will Huang Return?

The possibility of his return has gained traction in recent weeks. Several employees have written to the board urging it to reinstate him, while Huang has also expressed interest in returning. Media reports last week said he had even secured the support of some board members.

Trump’s post comes amid an accommodative position from the Republicans.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who last week said Nvidia should go with an outside hire, said on the weekend that the pick should depend on the outcome of investigations into who was responsible for Nvidia’s advanced chips being sold to China.

Speaking on the CBS program “Face the Nation,” Bessent downplayed concerns about Huang’s affair, suggesting that the relationship was a “canard” and that the corporate culture at Nvidia was more important than “one person’s foibles.”

On Sunday, prediction markets platform Kalshi said the odds of Huang’s return doubled in the week.

Nvidia Fallout

Nvidia’s stock decline notwithstand, the company faces a series of government probes. The Securities and Exchange Commission has reportedly opened an investigation into Nvidia’s accounting practices, days after California launched a probe into whether Nvidia misled investors with its business dealings in China.

The Justice and Commerce Departments said last week that they were pursuing a criminal investigation of Megaspeed, a Singapore company once led by Alice Huang, the woman whom U.S. officials believe worked as a Chinese intelligence asset while having an affair with Huang. Government officials are looking into whether Megaspeed smuggled Nvidia’s chips into China.

Retail View For NVDA

On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for NVDA was ‘extremely bullish,’ unchanged over the past week, with several traders highlighting Trump’s latest post.

“$NVDA When Jensen comes back, he’s gonna clean house and deal with every cheater who betrayed him. Time to change the whole damn kitchen,” said a trader.

Year to date, NVDA stock is down 32.5%.

data.title: Mahindra Finance Looking to Line Credit Business with Some Gold
data.description:
Sangita Mehta & Lijee Philip Mumbai: Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services is evaluating the acquisition of gold finance companies to accelerate its push into the segment, which is one of the fastest-growing, said people with knowledge of the matter. Among the companies being considered as potential acquisition targets are Indel Money, Kosamattam Finance, ICL Fincorp and Supra Pacific Financial Services. The company has initiated discussions but has yet to make any formal acquisition offers, the people said.

Mahindra Finance is 52.4% owned by automaker Mahindra & Mahindra that traditionally finances vehicles. Faster Scale-up10 The interest in gold loans comes as Mahindra Finance seeks to diversify its revenue streams and increase the share of non-vehicle businesses in its portfolio. The development comes amid a consolidation spree in the industry. The company denied it was in talks for a purchase deal.

Unlike several other lending products, gold loans require an extensive branch network, secure vault infrastructure and employees trained in valuation of the precious metal. "Buying an established lender would help Mahindra Finance scale up its gold loan business faster as it will get immediate access to infrastructure along with an experienced management team and an existing customer base," said one of the persons cited.

Among the companies being evaluated, Kosamattam Finance is the largest of the four and fully focused on gold loans. It had a loan book of Rs 8,130 crore at the end of June with about 1,000 branches. Indel Money has a pan-India presence and focuses solely on gold loans, with assets under management (AUM) of Rs 4,376 crore at the end of June and 440 branches. ICL Fincorp had a loan book of Rs 1,235 crore at the end of September and nearly 300 branches.

Mumbai-based Supra Pacific Financial Services has an AUM of about Rs 350 crore and 88 gold loan branches. The first three on the list are headquartered in Kerala. Mahindra Finance said in an email that "we would like to deny the information." Kosamattam Finance said, "We confirm there is no discussion happening from our side regarding acquisition from Mahindra Finance." Indel Money, ICL Fincorp and Supra Pacific Financial Services did not respond to queries.

Mahindra Finance already has an operational presence in the gold loan segment through Sri Lankan subsidiary Mahindra Ideal Finance. The company offers gold loans alongside vehicle financing and other lending products in the island nation. Mahindra Finance acquired a controlling 58.2% stake in the entity in July 2021. Speaking to analysts after the company's quarterly results, Mahindra Finance MD and CEO Raul Rebello said its asset base was becoming more diversified, with non-vehicle businesses such as SME loans, mortgages and personal loans contributing more to growth as vehicle lending continues to expand.

Vehicle loans account for 80% of Mahindra Finance's Rs 1.56 lakh crore AUM, with non-vehicle business accounting for the remaining 20%. While the price of the yellow metal has fallen in recent weeks, gold loans remain an attractive segment for lenders largely because they are fully secured and delinquencies are below 2%. The combined gold loan portfolio of banks and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) stands at about Rs 23 lakh crore, making it the second-largest retail lending product after home loans amid intensifying competition. The potential move by Mahindra Finance comes amid a wave of acquisitions in the gold loan business as NBFCs seek to grow inorganically.

Tata Play is seeking 1,500 crore for the business, which has around 650,000 subscribers, while ACT is willing to offer about 800 crore, according to people familiar with the matter.

Tata Play Broadband narrowed its net loss to 78 crore in FY26 from 101 crore in FY25, while revenue rose to 453 crore from 383 crore. ACT, which has around 2.5 million subscribers, reported revenue of 2,204 crore and net profit of 257 crore in FY25. It is India's largest non-telecom internet service provider. The proposed transaction comes amid mounting pressure on traditional television distribution businesses, prompting operators to explore adjacent segments such as broadband, OTT aggregation and linear TV streaming.

Tata Play has also recently undergone a leadership transition, with long-time MD and CEO Harit Nagpal retiring and joining the board. The company is evaluating candidates for the top job, sources said. The deal, if completed, is likely to be funded through ACT's internal accruals. The company had free cash and bank balances, unencumbered fixed deposits and investments totalling 1,324 crore as of December 31, 2025, against bank debt of 100 crore.

Emails sent to Tata Play and ACT seeking comments remained unanswered until press time. The proposed sale comes as Tata Play's core DTH business grapples with sustained subscriber losses. India's pay-DTH subscriber base fell from 56 million in April-June 2025 to 48.56 million in April-June 2026. Tata Play remains the market leader, with over 30% market share. The company widened its net loss by 4.2% to 551 crore in FY26 from 529 crore a year earlier, while revenue declined 13.5% to 3,530 crore.

Subscriber migration to DD Free Dish and streaming platforms such as Netflix, Prime Video, YouTube and JioHotstar has weighed on its business. The move also comes against the backdrop of consolidation in India's television distribution industry, which is facing declining pay-TV revenues and a shrinking subscriber base. Tata Play had earlier held discussions with Bharti Airtel on a possible merger of their respective DTH businesses, but the talks did not result in a transaction.

The proposed broadband sale signals a potential restructuring of Tata Play's portfolio as it navigates the structural decline of traditional television distribution. ACT, meanwhile, has been sharpening its focus on broadband. In June, it sold seven cable TV entities to GTPL Hathway for 36 crore. The businesses served around 600,000 subscribers across Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka and Odisha.

data.title: Coca-Cola to Revive the Gold Spot Moment
data.description:
after a 26-year gap... Ratna Bhushan New Delhi: Coca-Cola will revive its orange fizzy drink Gold Spot after 26 years amid an explosion of beverage rivals and the sugar-free rush in the market, people aware of the development said. The India unit of the Atlanta-based beverage maker acquired Gold Spot from Parle Bisleri owner Ramesh Chauhan in 1993 along with Thums Up and Limca. It discontinued Gold Spot soon after, to make way for its own global drink Fanta. "Gold Spot is returning as a low-sugar, no-sugar drink, so it won't cannibalise on Fanta.

It is expected to be on shelves starting next week," one of the executives aware of the developments, said. An email sent to Coca-Cola India remained unanswered till press time on Sunday. Over the weekend, social media posts showing former India cricket captain MS Dhoni and his wife seen with Gold Spot cans went viral. It is not clear if the cricketer has been signed to endorse the brand.

Gold Spot, which had the tagline 'zing thing', was phased out by Coca-Cola in 2000 to make way for its own global brand Fanta. "Market share gain of legacy brands being revived after a long gap depends entirely on adequate investments in distribution, product and go-to-market," the executive cited above said. "Some like Thums Up, however, have always led the Indian cola market, ahead of Coca-Cola's own global brand Coke as well as rival Pepsi, even without investments in the early years." However, unlike colas which dominate the 60,000 aerated drinks category, orange remains a relatively smaller segment of the total mix.

The revival comes as demand shifts sharply toward healthier options with New Delhi's proposed regulatory norm of requiring red hexagonal labels on all front-packs of foods and beverages to declare excess quantities of sugar, salt and fats, and stiff competition. Rivals such as Reliance Consumer Products' Campa, Lahori Zeera, Bindu Zeera and newer entrants such as ITC's Coconut Cola and Zyro by Veera Foods, have been challenging the dominance of Coca-Cola and PepsiCo in recent months for the first time in India.

Meanwhile, sales of Coca-Cola's mid-calorie and no-sugar drinks, which include zero- or no-sugar brands under flagship Coke, Sprite and Thums Up, in addition to Schweppes, Powerade and Rimzim, have doubled this year over the last, two bottling industry associates said. Diet and light drinks now make over 60% of Coca-Cola's total annual sales, compared to about 30% last year, they said. Rival PepsiCo's bottling associate Varun Beverages reported that sales of its zero-sugar and low-sugar drinks doubled to 88% of total volumes in the July-September 2026 quarter, up from 44% a year earlier. The mix also includes water and sodas.

data.title: Select HFCs Offer Rate Cuts, Top-ups to Retain Borrowers
data.description:
Saloni Shukla Mumbai: Housing finance companies are increasingly offering interest rate concessions, pre-approved top-up loans and personalised retention incentives to prevent borrowers from shifting their mortgages to rival lenders. The measures are starting to yield results after heightened balance-transfer activity earlier this year. Several housing financiers have contained customer exits through targeted interventions amid intense competition from banks and other mortgage lenders.

Home First Finance lowered its balance-transfer outflow rate to around 4.5% from 5-6% previously, while Aadhar Housing Finance and India Shelter Finance reported a 40-basis-point year-on-year cut each, to 5.1% and 4%, respectively. "Spending the time to explain the customer itself saves us some balance transfers," managing director Manoj Viswanathan said. He said the lender has introduced a multi-step retention process involving direct engagement with borrowers, explaining the costs of refinancing, offering top-up loans, and finally providing interest-rate concessions. These initiatives have helped reduce outflows, although management expects the rate to remain within a 4-6% range.

data.title: Electrolyser Cos Seek Approved List of Suppliers to Ramp up Local Sourcing
data.description:
Kalpana Pathak Mumbai: Electrolyser manufacturers urged the Centre to create an approved list of domestic manufacturers on the lines of the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) for solar modules to ensure green hydrogen projects and public sector companies source equipment from homegrown suppliers. This comes amid concerns over weak local electrolyser demand and more than a dozen companies investing in manufacturing facilities under the production linked incentive (PLI) scheme.

Manufacturers fear without assured orders, the sector could face a capacity glut even as companies continue to bear the costs of setting up factories. "Industry players have been raising the proposal individually at government roundtables and industry forums, seeking a domestic sourcing requirement for buyers, including public sector oil companies such as Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum Corporation and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation," said an industry executive part of the discussions.

He said an ALMM-like mechanism could help create a market for locally produced electrolysers and reduce dependence on imported equipment, particularly from China. More than 20 companies including Reliance Industries, John Cockerill Greenko Hydrogen, Advait Infratech, Homi Hydrogen, L&T Electrolysers and Adani New Industries, among others had won the PLI bid to set up electrolyser manufacturing facilities in the country.

The industry demand comes at a time when the award of green ammonia projects has yet to translate into significant equipment orders. Developers are still working towards financial closure and are yet to place orders with electrolyser manufacturers. Equipment procurement could happen only around two to two-and-a-half years after project awards, leaving manufacturers with a long wait for demand to materialise.

The weak order pipeline has also raised questions about the viability of the country's expanding electrolyser manufacturing capacity. Around 11-12 companies have been selected in the first and second tranches of the PLI scheme to support domestic manufacturing. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) didn't respond to email queries. MNRE has given manufacturers under the first tranche flexibility to commission their facilities by August 2027.

Companies without immediate orders can defer the start of their PLI incentive period so they don't lose the initial incentive years while production remains idle. However, manufacturers said the timeline flexibility alone won't address the demand problem. Since the PLI scheme is linked to actual production, companies won't get incentives in the absence of orders and output.

data.title: Page Inds Looks to Stitch Together Growth with New Launches, Wider Distribution
data.description:
Snehal Mergu ET Intelligence Group: Shares of Page Industries trade near their 52-week low after falling sharply over the past week amid lakclustre sales volume growth and weaker operating margin in the September quarter. Although the company, which is an exclusive licensee of innerwear maker Jockey International in India, has retained the double-digit volume growth guidance for FY27 backed by new product launches and festive demand, investors remain unconvinced.

The stock has lost 15% in the past seven trading sessions following the quarterly results as clocking double-digit volume growth seems tough given the weak trend in the first half of the year. This combined with a persistent input cost inflation has prompted analysts to cut price targets for the stock by as much as 25%. Despite that, the potential upside for the stock remains around 29% from the current level of 31,000, reflecting optimism backed by rising capacity utilisation and expanding distribution network.

Adding to investor concerns is a compliance issue related to the Foreign Exchange Management (FEMA) act involving about 48 crore of transactions. Though the company expects no operational impact and a likely penalty of around 0.75% of the amount involved, the maximum statutory downside could be three times the amount. According to tax experts, the matter does not, by itself, imply any additional income-tax liability.

However, the financial impact will depend on whether authorities determine that a FEMA contravention occurred. Page has clocked 5.6% volume growth in the first half of FY27, making it a daunting task to meet the management's volume guidance. JM Financial estimates that volumes need to grow around 14% in the second half to meet the target, which it considers challenging.

While the company has raised product prices, input cost inflation has risen at a faster rate. As a result, operating margin before depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda margin) slipped to 20.8% in the September quarter from 21.7% a year earlier. The company has maintained the 19-21% Ebitda margin guidance for FY27, with another price increase remaining an option if cost inflation persists.

The company plans to add 8,000-10,000 outlets in FY27, expanding a network that already spans 115,426 multi-brand outlets, 1,662 exclusive brand stores and 921 large-format stores. Capacity ramp-up at the Odisha and Karnataka plants by the end of FY28 from the current levels of around 40% will likely ease supply constraints. Analysts remain cautious on Page Industries' near-term outlook, with JM Financial and Emkay Global Financial Services cutting earnings estimates and target prices after weak volume growth and persistent input-cost pressure. However, brokerages remain constructive on the long-term story, with stock price targets going up to 40,000, supported by distribution expansion, category premiumisation, and better capacity utilisation.

data.title: GCCs Turn Eastward to Tap Kolkata's Growing Education Hub Talent Base
data.description:
Beena Parmar Bengaluru: As multinationals look to diversify their technology and global capability centres (GCCs), eastern India's West Bengal, more precisely Kolkata, is among the cities that is gaining traction. Earlier this year, Cushman & Wakefield's latest office market data highlighted that Kolkata saw a 239% year-on-year growth in GCC gross leasing volume (GLV) to 0.5 million sqft (5 lakh sqft) in 2025 up from 0.1 million MSF (1.5 lakh sqft) in 2024. decisive phase In recent years, as technology and talent made advances alongside rising costs, Indian GCCs have entered a more decisive phase beyond being cost hubs to more research and higher value-driven centres.

West Bengal is now emerging as a complement to the Tier-1 hubs rather than a challenger, says Arindam Sen, Partner and GCC Sector Leader (TMT), EY India. "Kolkata's edge is a cost-talent equation that still works, comparatively lower operating costs and significantly lower attrition than Tier-1 hubs, a deep and loyal talent pool from IIT Kharagpur, IIM Calcutta, ISI and Jadavpur University, and strengthening infrastructure in Sector V and New Town," Sen said.

The eastern state also draws on IIT Kharagpur, IIM Calcutta, the Indian Statistical Institute and Jadavpur University, alongside a wide network of engineering, science and commerce colleges, with growing depth across IT, engineering, analytics and business processes management (BPM), Sen added. To be sure, numbers are still very small as compared to the bigger cities like Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Delhi and Mumbai.

More than 20 multinational GCCs are already operating in Kolkata, including the likes of HSBC, Ericsson and BT Group, EY-ASSOCHAM's assessment identified. "Most already run mature centres elsewhere in India and have added Kolkata deliberately, to diversify risk and access a fresh talent pool," Sen said. India is home to around 2,117 GCC units with a direct and indirect employed workforce of 2.36 million.

The market revenue of the Indian units stood at $98.4 billion at the end of fiscal year to March 2026. While Kolkata's contribution is not substantial overall, 12 companies have a Kolkata-only GCC where software testing, customer success, cyber, application development, and business intelligence are part of the work , said Rohan Lobo, partner and TMT Industry Leader, Deloitte South Asia. India's GCC ecosystem is entering a decisive phase with the onset of AI. As enterprises move from cost-led delivery models to research and intelligence-led operating models, GCCs are being repositioned as engines of enterprise transformation.

AI, data and automation are no longer incremental enablers; they now define how work is structured, governed and scaled, shaping intelligence-led GCCs in India. Lobo notes that customer service is one area to pay particular attention to in West Bengal. "With the right investment in English communication, domain skills and AI, we are seeing a strong workforce capable of supporting increasingly complex global customer operations," he said, adding that local IT firms and the ecosystem at large, especially in AI skills, also have an important role to play.

Today, multinationals are looking to move their work inwards with more insourcing through GCCs tapping India's scalable talent and technology. Lobo notes that Kolkata has a robust IT services ecosystem that drives GCCs, and the state government is actively trying to push India's north-east for customer care and support services because they have good English. Sharp rise in leasing Kolkata is also witnessing a sharp rise in the growth of GCC office leasing with IT and business process management accounting for nearly 50-60% of that activity, Lobo said. "The opportunity for West Bengal is not to replicate Bengaluru or Hyderabad.

It is to identify where it can genuinely compete, build those capabilities at scale, and give global companies a compelling reason to invest." The city's strengths are tangible, says Mohith Mohan, founder and CEO of GCC enabler MOAR Advisory. "Grade-A rents at about 40% of those in typical Tier 1 cities give enterprises room to build thoughtfully rather than conservatively.

IIT Kharagpur, IIM Calcutta, and several other institutions provide a strong talent pipeline across engineering, analytics, and finance," Mohan said. Mohan pointed to recent developments around the business delivery centre of Tata Steel evolving into a GCC, Visteon's plans to have 300 engineers in Kolkata by the end of 2026 and with New Town's data-centre cluster adding capacity, enterprises are moving increasingly complex work to West Bengal.

The new Investment Promotion Policy also sends a constructive signal. "The next stage is about depth and readiness. That means industry-designed programmes in AI, data, cybersecurity, and product engineering, along with pathways for professionals to return to the region," Mohan added. (ET's Bengal Ascends summit in Kolkata on November 24 will bring together policymakers, industrialists and technocrats to deliberate on the agenda for an ascending Bengal.)

data.title: Pernod Ricard Plans IPO for 'Absolutely Strategic' India Unit
data.description:
Sagar Malviya Mumbai: French distiller Pernod Ricard's board may meet in India in January to discuss a potential listing of the local entity, said chairman Alexandre Ricard, underscoring the growing strategic importance of a market that could eventually overtake the US as its single largest globally. The grandson of the group founder told shareholders at an annual general meeting Friday that preparatory work for the initial public offering (IPO) is underway.

On a shareholder query about whether the group's centre of gravity in Asia is shifting "from the Yangtze towards the Ganga", Ricard said, "India is absolutely strategic". He, however, forewarned that a listing would bring greater bureaucracy and complexity to the Indian business and entail an irreversible dilution of the parent's ownership.

The maker of Chivas Regal, Royal Stag and The Glenlivet highlighted rising economic nationalism and consumer preference for locally produced brands in emerging markets such as India, China and Africa. "There is a real rise of patriotism and locally produced," he said. The Indian market has in the past decade undergone a transformation-from mass-market blended whiskies to locally produced 100% single malts.

Foreign distillers Pernod and rival Diageo developed their own single malts in India. Ricard was referring to what he called the "dewesternisation" of the company's strategy, including collaborations with local artists and stronger local connections for international brands."This narrative of a local anchor is very important," he said, adding that a stock market listing could strengthen relationships with regulators, customers, suppliers and other partners.

It could also make the Indian unit more attractive to talent. Speaking at the AGM, a shareholder suggested a more than $1 billion IPO, but Ricard didn't confirm the size. The board had asked him about a year ago to examine the strategic rationale for listing the Indian affiliate, and the company is undertaking preparatory work to preserve the option. The next board meeting in January could be held in India, subject to geopolitical developments, he said.

The proposed listing would require Pernod to dilute its ownership to about 75%, with Indian regulations mandating a minimum 25% public float. While a listing could strengthen governance, transparency and local stakeholder relationships, it would also mean surrendering exclusive ownership and accepting greater regulatory and administrative complexity. "When you have flexibility, agility, and the possibility to make a mistake and then to walk it back, it's one thing," he said. "But when we know that if this decision was to be taken, it would be absolutely irreversible, irrevocable." Pernod will also face additional bureaucracy, he said, emphasising that the board would need to be convinced of the strategic benefits and favourable market conditions before proceeding with the IPO. The Indian market has attained a meteoric rise within Pernod's global operations.

Ricard said the country was not even among the group's top 12 markets when he joined but has progressively climbed the ranks to become its second-largest after the US and one of its four key regions. "If we carry out medium-term projections, even with a US market that will most likely pick up one day, India will overtake the US market in terms of revenue," he said.

Pernod reported a 0.9% decline in first-quarter sales despite contractions in the US and China, with India contributing significantly to offsetting the weakness. Pernod Ricard India reported FY26 revenue excluding excise duty of 13,315 crore, up 0.6%. Profit before exceptional items and tax rose 5.7% to 2,483 crore. Net profit surged to 4,559 crore from 1,755 crore, boosted by a 3,223-crore gain from the sale of Imperial Blue to Tilaknagar Industries.

data.title: In its Third Attempt, Oyo Parent Targets Q4 Launch of Public Issue
data.description:
Pranav Mukul & Samidha Sharma New Delhi | Mumbai: Oravel Stays, the parent company of hospitality firm Oyo, is likely to launch its initial public offering (IPO) in the January-March quarter, with its valuation being pegged at 20,000-22,000 crore ($2.1-2.3 billion), people briefed on the matter said. The valuation being offered by public market investors is almost flat compared with the $2.3 billion at which the Gurugram-based company had last raised capital two years ago.

This is Oyo's third attempt at going public, and the Ritesh Agarwal-founded company is expected to file a revised draft prospectus in the coming weeks, said one of the persons. In an October filing, Oravel had cut its proposed IPO size by nearly half to 3,350 crore, amid a recalibration of its fundraising plans. The hospitality firm's IPO is expected to be entirely a primary capital raise, with none of the shareholders selling stakes through an offer-for-sale (OFS) component. "The company's representatives are meeting potential institutional investors, and the final pricing is subject to change closer to the IPO launch," said one of the people cited. "It is targeting a pre-money valuation of 24,000 crore, but large domestic funds are pricing it at around 20,000-22,000 crore." Axis Capital, Citi, Goldman Sachs, InCred Capital, Intensive Fiscal Services, JM Financial and SBI Capital Markets are bankers to the Oravel Stays Ltd public issue.

Responding to ET's queries, a company spokesperson said, "The public issue timeline and valuation mentioned by you are inaccurate. We will share when we have any update." The company's first attempt at going public began in September 2021, when it filed for a 8,430-crore ($1.2 billion) IPO. In December 2022, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) returned the draft prospectus and asked the company to refile it with updated financials.

Oyo then made a confidential filing in March 2023 for a significantly smaller issue of $400-600 million. In May 2024, the company withdrew that filing and opted for a private funding round instead. For its third attempt, the company made a fresh confidential filing in December 2025, followed by an updated draft prospectus in June 2026 after receiving clearance from Sebi. At the time of its confidential filing, Oyo was targeting a valuation of $5-7 billion (45,000-46,000 crore), ET had reported.

Bloomberg had reported on October 23 that the company's valuation was likely to be lower than its initial targets. Majority biz outside India In its annual report for FY26, Oravel reported operating revenue of 9,358 crore, up 50% year-on-year. Net profit more than quadrupled to 994 crore in FY26 from 245 crore the previous year, aided by a 678 crore deferred-tax credit. The company said it benefited from higher business volumes, a stronger contribution from premium and company-serviced hotels, operating leverage across markets and the full-year contribution from US motel chain G6 Hospitality, which it acquired in December 2024.

Oravel ran 22,769 hotels on its platform, excluding G6 properties, as of FY26, compared with 12,971 in FY23, according to the annual report. Once driven primarily by its Oyo-branded hotels in India, the company has increasingly expanded its international footprint. More than 84% of its operating revenue now comes from outside India, with the US contributing 27% and Europe around 24%. In September 2025, the parent company rebranded itself as Prism to reflect its consolidated global brands beyond Oyo.

data.title: Buy the house or buy into a fund?
data.description:
For most Indian families, buying a home abroad has followed a life event, such as a child going overseas to study or the family planning a move. That is changing. More Indians now buy property abroad as an investment, spreading their wealth across countries and earning rent in a foreign currency. Dubai remains the clear favourite. Indians made up about 20-22% of foreign property buyers there in 2025, says Aayush Puri, CEO-Residential, Middle East and CEO, Anarock Channel Partners.

He credits its proximity, the dirham's peg to the US dollar and rental yields well above the 2-3% typical in India. Some also buy for residency. Dubai, for instance, offers a property-linked Golden Visa route with a minimum qualifying investment of AED 2 million (Rs 5.01 crore), says Prateek Pant, Market Head-Middle East and Africa, ASK Private Wealth. Where buyers go depends on how much they spend, says Ritesh Mehta, Head-North, West & East, Residential Advisory Services, India, JLL (right graphic).

A. Balasubramanian, MD and CEO, Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC, sees a broader change in mindset. "The focus is increasingly moving towards evaluating overseas investments on their financial merit, including potential returns, risk diversification, liquidity and their contribution to long-term portfolio objectives." That raises a question: is buying a property still the best way to get this exposure?

What you own The answer starts with what the investor actually holds. "Direct ownership gives you title. You control the asset, decide when to sell, and bear every liability, from tenant disputes to local property taxes and succession in a foreign legal system," says Aditya Bhattacharya, Partner at King Stubb and Kasiva. Holding through a company, trust, Real Estate Investment Trust (Reit) or fund changes the nature of what you own.

You no longer own the building. "You own shares or units, which give you a contractual claim on income and exit proceeds, with limited say in how the asset is run," says Bhattacharya. A listed Reit holds income-producing a special purpose vehicle or merely a claim on the platform. Inside a fund Pagani Capital Fund shows how a private overseas fund works. It is a closed-ended Portuguese fund regulated by CMVM, Portugal's market regulator, and it backs a focused hospitality investment.

The project is a hotel being planned in the Algarve, on Portugal's southern coast, which will operate under Accor's MGallery Collection brand. The fund does not directly own the hotel building. It invests in the Portuguese hospitality business through equity and debt, including convertible bonds. So, investors own fund units, not rooms. "It is a concentrated strategy, so the quality of the operating business and its cash generation are central," says Joao Pagani Toscano, Founder and CEO, Pagani Capital.

Returns depend on how the hospitality business performs: occupancy, room rates, margins and capital expenditure, as well as how and when the underlying investment is repaid or sold. Class B and C investors have priority in the fund's liquidation waterfall. After invested capital is returned in the prescribed order, profits are allocated to these classes towards a 5.5% annualised return before remaining profits go to Class A. This is a distribution priority, not a guarantee.

Pagani Capital set up the fund, but it does not manage or hold its assets alone. A separate firm manages it, a Portuguese bank acts as depository, and an outside auditor checks the accounts. The fund's assets are segregated from the manager's own assets. Units are valued every six months, but that value is an estimate, not necessarily a price at which investors can sell. Getting out is the hard part.

data.title: Dollar edges off 19-month high after market rout; yen softens
data.description:
Key points:
  • Fed funds futures imply traders expect central bank still on track to hike 25bps
  • Aussie rallies after nine-day losing streak, kiwi struggles near 17-year low
  • Yen softens as safe-haven bid eases; Japan on holiday

By Gregor Stuart Hunter

The dollar eased off its highest in 19 months in Asian trade on Monday as investor confidence recovered after a selloff last week and traders pared bets that the Federal Reserve could hike interest rates aggressively at its meeting next month.

The euro was up 0.1% at $1.0985, while the British pound was 0.1% firmer at $1.3111, both up for a second day.

"Two weeks ago, hawkish Federal Reserve rhetoric pushed US yields higher and lifted the USD against developed-market currencies," OCBC analysts wrote in a note. "Over the past week, however, the rates shock evolved into a growth shock."

The New Zealand dollar fluctuated between gains and losses, last down 0.1% at $0.5468, falling for a 10th day and reaching its weakest since the midst of the global financial crisis in March 2009.

"Most of the weakness in the kiwi this year does seem to reflect the adverse shift in rate differentials, but the latest leg down looks like more of a traditional 'risk-off' move based on the developments in the stock market," said Thomas Mathews, head of markets for Asia Pacific at Capital Economics in Wellington.

The kiwi's Australian counterpart was 0.4% stronger at $0.66415, rebounding after nine consecutive days of loss.

The US dollar was 0.3% stronger against the yen at 158.95 yen as a safe-haven bid for the Japanese currency eased, with markets in the country closed for a holiday on Monday.

The US dollar index , which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was down 0.1% at 103.72, retreating further from a high last Thursday that was its strongest since April 2025, prior to the "Liberation Day" tariff announcement.

"We expect the USD to continue to outperform," said Eric Robertsen, global head of foreign exchange, rates and credit research at Standard Chartered in Dubai, citing the interest rate differentials, signs of strong productivity gains in the US economy and a relative decline in political risk compared to other countries such as France.

"If global risk aversion were to pick up, the USD should benefit as well," he said.

After last week's market rout, aggressive action from the Fed to fight inflation looks to be off the table.

Fed funds futures are pricing an implied 93.5% probability of a 25-basis-point hike at the US central bank's December 8-9 policy meeting, compared with a 6.5% chance of a hold, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool. A larger 50-basis-point increase, seen as carrying an 11.5% likelihood a week ago, is now completely priced out.

data.title: India could gain from Nvidia's weakening competitive edge in AI: William Lee
data.description:
India could emerge as an alternative destination for US chip exports and data centers amid growing uncertainty over the global artificial intelligence (AI) trade, says William Lee, Chief Economist and Managing Director, Global Economic Advisors.

He believes the country's large pool of software engineers and technology talent could also help companies transition from Nvidia chips to alternatives from AMD and Google. However, India will need to build greater trust with the US Commerce Department to attract these opportunities.

Lee says the AI trade is shifting beyond chips and software to financing, a transition he describes as moving from “chips to code and now to credit”. Nvidia's growing role in financing hyperscalers and startups has added to investor concerns about the sustainability of the AI boom.

He believes the resulting market turmoil could create opportunities for Nvidia's competitors and give India a chance to strengthen its position in the global AI supply chain.

data.title: ESDS Software clarifies on Sydney AI factory reports; stock extends losses
data.description:
Shares of ESDS Software Solutions Ltd. erased its early gains on Monday, November 23, after the company clarified that its Sydney AI factory project remains on schedule, with all 8,208 NVIDIA B300 GPUs installed and undergoing final testing.

The company said the entire capacity at the facility has been contracted to customers on a take-or-pay basis, with handover expected by mid-December 2026. Billing is scheduled to begin in January 2027.

In a clarification on its agreement with Sharon AI and the Sydney project, ESDS said the delivery timeline had been revised by mutual agreement with the partner. The revised schedule is also in line with the timeline Sharon AI disclosed alongside its quarterly results on November 16. ESDS said it opted to complete testing of the entire GPU cluster before taking handover.

The company said the revised schedule would not increase its costs, as payments to Sharon AI and corresponding receipts from customers will begin only after the cluster is accepted.

It added that the deposit placed with Sharon AI is refundable if the partner fails to meet its contractual delivery obligations.

ESDS said its financial commitment to Sharon AI, as disclosed in its prospectus, stands at approximately $1.26 billion over 60 months, translating into monthly payments of around $21 million. The amount is based on a fixed rate per GPU per hour for the duration of the contract.

The company clarified that the ₹3,000 crore annual cost mentioned during its November 2 earnings call was an approximation, while the contractual commitment works out to approximately $21 million a month.

On the revenue side, ESDS expects to receive around $30 million per month from customers for the Sydney project, against payments of approximately $21 million to Sharon AI. This would leave about $9 million a month before operating expenses and taxes.

Based on the contractual terms, the company currently estimates monthly profit after tax of around $4-5 million, translating into a margin of approximately 14–17% of revenue.

ESDS said the entire capacity of the Sydney facility has been contracted to customers under take-or-pay agreements. This means customers are required to pay for the committed capacity irrespective of actual utilisation.

The company added that the duration and exit provisions of customer agreements are aligned with its contract with Sharon AI, limiting its exposure to the risk of low utilisation. Customers have also made upfront payments, it said, while their identities remain confidential under contractual terms.

The company further clarified that it had placed a cash deposit of $140 million, equivalent to ₹1,336 crore, with Sharon AI in May 2026 instead of providing letters of credit. It said no additional letter of credit or bank guarantee is outstanding or required.

According to ESDS, the deposit was funded through a $140 million advance received from customers and did not require the use of its own cash. The amount will be adjusted against service fees over the contract period and is classified as an advance to vendor.

The customer advances reflected in the company's balance sheet as of September 30, 2026, include amounts received before March 31, 2026, which were disclosed in its prospectus, as well as the $140 million advance used to fund the deposit with Sharon AI.

ESDS said the earlier advances remain unutilised in the group's bank accounts and that it did not receive any significant additional customer advances during the September quarter.

On its role in the project, ESDS said Sharon AI owns the hardware and data centre capacity, while the company will provide customers with a managed service covering cluster operations, round-the-clock network and security monitoring, model training and GPU-as-a-Service.

These services will be offered under a single contract, with ESDS acting as the accountable service provider.

The arrangement allows the company to expand its capacity without making substantial investments in land, buildings or GPU hardware, while continuing to develop its own GPU infrastructure in India.

ESDS said it will inform the stock exchanges once the Sydney AI factory becomes operational and make further disclosures as required under Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) regulations.

The company also cautioned that payments to Sharon AI and receipts from customers are denominated in US dollars. While currency movements could affect the rupee value of reported revenue, costs and profits, ESDS said they would not change the margin earned in dollar terms. The project timelines and profit estimates remain expectations and are not guaranteed.

ESDS Software Solutions shares opened as much as 2% higher on Monday, November 23, following the clarification.
